summary: Sam van Schaik is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Manchester (~1996–2000) and studied under Lama Jampa Thaye, Karma Thinley Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga. He held posts at the British Library and SOAS.

Samani Pratibha Pragya works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (2011–2017), where she also served as a research assistant (attested 2020).

Sambhavi Ganesh studied at Lady Shri Ram College, the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, and the University of Edinburgh (PhD 2020–2024 under Radhika Govinda). She worked at Kudumbashree National Resource Organisation and became a teaching assistant at King's College London (2025–2026).

Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He held a post at the University of Calcutta and served as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Sampadananda Mishra is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Pondicherry University. He served as Director at Rishihood University (2021) and became a Professor at the Hindu University of America in 2022.
Sampan Chakrabarty studied under doctoral supervisor Pallab Sengupta. He has served as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026), working in Indology.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay works in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London (PhD under David Snellgrove), he held posts at SOAS, Collège de France, CNRS, Paris Nanterre University, and the International Association for Tibetan Studies.

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, and Durham University, he served as headmaster at Bramham College, worked for the India Office Records, and was Professor of Chinese at University College London.

Samuel Charles Hill was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at University College London, he served in the Bengal Educational Service (1881–1912), as Professor at Dhaka College, and was in charge at the National Archives of India.
Samuel Charters Macpherson was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Edinburgh (1822–1823) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1823–1827).

Samuel De Coster Atkins was an Indologist and linguist who earned his A.B. and Ph.D. from Princeton University. After serving as an assistant at Baylor University (1935–1937), he was Assistant Professor of Classics and Sanskrit at Princeton University (1937–1978).

Samuel George Frederick Brandon was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds and held an academic post at the University of Manchester (~1951–1971).

Samuel Gottlieb Rudolf Henzi studied at Bern, Tübingen, and Göttingen, and with Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. In 1820, he became Professor of Exegesis and Oriental Languages at the University of Tartu, working in religious studies.

Samuel Grant Oliphant was an Indologist and linguist educated at Princeton and Johns Hopkins (PhD under Maurice Bloomfield). He taught at Parsons College, Phillips Exeter, Johns Hopkins, The University of Olivet, Washington & Jefferson, and Grove City College.
Samuel Heinrich Ribbach was a scholar in Tibetology. He served as a missionary for the Moravian Church from 1892 to 1927 and held a post at the Museum am Rothenbaum.
Samuel Henry Butcher was educated at Marlborough College and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Edinburgh (~1882–1903) and Harvard University (~1904).

Samuel Henry Kellogg was an Indologist and linguist educated at Princeton University and Princeton Theological Seminary. He served as an instructor at Allahabad Theological Training School (1873–1876) and Professor of Systematic Theology at Pittsburgh Theological Seminary (1877–1885).
Samuel Johnson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge, and Pembroke College, Oxford.

Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Central Asian and Iranian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
Samuel Mateer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Bedford Theological College (~1858–1859). He served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society from 1859 to 1891.
